pack.title: Chronic borrowers
pack.description: Get a borrowed item returned before lending more.

scenarios.setting: A neighbor asks to borrow your drill again before returning your ladder.
scenarios.jab: Can I grab your drill? I'll bring everything back later.
scenarios.goal: Get a borrowed item returned before lending more.

replies.line: Please return the ladder first; I'm not lending anything else today.
replies.why: It ties the current request to a specific outstanding return without adding accusations.
replies.delivery: Keep “return the ladder” specific; don't list every past favor.

replies.line: Ladder back first. No drill today.
replies.why: It names both the next action and today's lending limit.
replies.delivery: Say “Ladder back first” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. Don't list every past favor.

replies.line: Could you bring the ladder back today? I'd like to keep my tools at home for now.
replies.why: It asks for the return while explaining your current lending boundary.
replies.delivery: Keep “Could you bring the ladder back today” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. Don't list every past favor.

replies.line: The ladder needs to come home before anyone else gets a field trip.
replies.why: The playful image makes the return sequence clear without calling the neighbor irresponsible.
replies.delivery: Keep “The ladder needs to come home before anyone” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. Don't list every past favor.

followUp.jab: You're acting like I stole it.
followUp.line: I'm asking for my ladder back; I'm not accusing you of stealing.
followUp.why: It clarifies the request and avoids adopting the accusation frame.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “I'm asking for my ladder back,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
